h2: Septic & Sewer Canggu – Fast Fixes for Villa Owners
intro: If your villa in Berawa or Batu Bolong is throwing off a sewer smell, backing up after rain, or draining slowly, the underground plumbing is likely under pressure from high groundwater and fast-built pipework. I diagnose the source, arrange tank pumping, and clear blocked lines so the problem doesn't return next monsoon.

sections.h3: Why Canggu's Groundwater Makes Septics Work Harder
sections.text: Most plots here were rice paddies until a few years ago, which means the water table sits close to the surface. A standard septic tank fills noticeably faster than one on dry soil, and drains can back up within hours of heavy rain. When a villa was built quickly over former paddy land, the original slope calculations rarely account for that extra saturation, so slow drains and a persistent odour near the soakaway are common complaints in the first two or three seasons.

sections.h3: What Usually Goes Wrong Around Pererenan and Babakan
sections.text: Walk through any new-build street in Pererenan or Babakan and you'll find loose fittings, hidden hairline leaks behind tile work, and grease traps that were never sized correctly for daily guest use. The most frequent call-outs I see: a foul smell drifting into the living area after cooking, a toilet that gurgles and barely flushes, a kitchen drain that stops mid-meal, and a sewer line that has collapsed where it meets the municipal connection. Each one needs a different fix, but they all start with finding the exact point of failure before calling a pump truck.

sections.h3: Send Photos on WhatsApp for a Quick Quote
sections.text: No need to describe the problem in long paragraphs. Snap a photo of the affected drain, the pump room, or the spot where the smell is strongest, add a short note about when it started, and send it over on WhatsApp. Pricing depends entirely on what's wrong—a simple trap clear is very different from excavating a collapsed pipe—so I'll look at your photos, tell you what I think the issue is, and give you a figure before anyone picks up a tool. You approve, then we schedule.

sections.h3: Prevention Tips Before the Rainy Season Hits
sections.text: Between April and October, take ten minutes each week to check that your sump pump still kicks on, the pool overflow channel isn't choked with leaves from the surrounding fields, and nothing is pooling around the septic lid. In Canggu the rain arrives fast and stays for days; a pump that seized in May will flood your ground floor by November. A quick visual inspection now saves an emergency call-out later, especially if your villa sits low relative to the street.

faq.q: How often should a villa septic tank be pumped out?
faq.a: With Canggu's high water table, most tanks need pumping every 12–18 months rather than the 3-year interval people expect on dry land. If you notice slower drains or a faint odour, don't wait—the next heavy rain will push it over the edge.

faq.q: Can you clear a blocked sewer line without digging up the garden?
faq.a: In many cases yes: a flexible camera snake locates the blockage and clears it through the existing access point. If the pipe has actually collapsed under the lawn, I'll show you the footage first so you can decide whether a targeted patch repair makes sense before any major excavation.

faq.q: Do you handle grease traps at villas with a small kitchen or café setup?
faq.a: Yes—grease-trap cleaning and clearing are part of what I do. Send a photo of the trap unit and how full it looks on WhatsApp, and I'll let you know whether it needs a simple flush or a full pump-out and reset.
